VoiceChannel.title: VoiceChannel
VoiceChannel.description: Represents a static voice communication channel within the Kanka Voice application. These channels are predefined and serve as gathering points for users to engage in peer-to-peer voice chat.

id.description: Unique identifier for the VoiceChannel entity. This would typically be a static, system-defined ID (e.g., 'genel', 'oyun').

name.description: The user-facing display name of the voice channel (e.g., 'Genel', 'Oyun', 'Muhabbet').

UserPresence.title: UserPresence
UserPresence.description: Tracks a user's active presence in a specific voice channel. This entity is crucial for the WebRTC signaling process, allowing users in a channel to discover and connect with each other, and for displaying 'online' users in the UI.

id.description: Unique identifier for this UserPresence record. This could be a combination of userId and voiceChannelId or a generated UUID for the session.

userId.description: The unique local identifier for the user, typically generated and stored in localStorage upon login.

displayName.description: The display name of the user as entered and stored in localStorage.

voiceChannelId.description: Reference to the VoiceChannel the user is currently present in. (Relationship: VoiceChannel 1:N UserPresence)

lastSeen.description: Timestamp indicating the last time this presence record was updated, useful for identifying and cleaning up stale or disconnected users.

isMuted.description: Indicates if the user's microphone is currently muted.

isKicked.description: Indicates if the user has been kicked from the channel by an admin.

WebRTCSignal.title: WebRTCSignal
WebRTCSignal.description: Stores transient WebRTC signaling messages (offers, answers, ICE candidates) exchanged between users via Firestore to establish and maintain peer-to-peer connections for voice chat. These messages are typically short-lived.

id.description: Unique identifier for the WebRTCSignal entity. This will be a Firestore document ID or a generated UUID.

senderUserId.description: The unique local identifier of the user who initiated and sent this signaling message.

receiverUserId.description: The unique local identifier of the user who is the intended recipient of this signaling message.

voiceChannelId.description: Reference to the VoiceChannel where this signaling exchange is taking place. Ensures signals are scoped to the correct channel. (Relationship: VoiceChannel 1:N WebRTCSignal)

signalType.description: The type of WebRTC signal being sent (e.g., 'offer', 'answer', 'iceCandidate').

signalData.description: The actual payload of the WebRTC signaling message, typically a stringified JSON object containing SDP or ICE candidate information.

timestamp.description: The date and time when the signaling message was created, useful for ordering and potential cleanup of old signals.

definition.description: Stores static, predefined voice communication channels. This collection is globally readable, allowing any user to discover available channels.

params.name: voiceChannelId
params.description: The unique identifier for the voice channel (e.g., 'genel', 'oyun').

definition.description: Tracks a user's active presence in a specific voice channel. Documents include `userId`, `displayName`, `voiceChannelId`, and `lastSeen`. The `userId` in the path corresponds to the `userId` in the document for ownership. Includes denormalized `userId` and `voiceChannelId` for Authorization Independence and QAP-compliant listing.

params.name: voiceChannelId
params.description: The unique identifier of the voice channel the user is present in.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique local identifier for the user (from localStorage).

definition.description: Stores transient WebRTC signaling messages (offers, answers, ICE candidates) for a specific `receiverUserId` within a `voiceChannelId`. This acts as a 'mailbox' for the receiver. Documents include `senderUserId`, `receiverUserId`, `voiceChannelId`, `signalType`, `signalData`, and `timestamp`. The `receiverUserId` in the path ensures that only the intended recipient can read their signals. `senderUserId` is denormalized in the document for write authorization. `voiceChannelId` is denormalized in the path and document for Authorization Independence and scoping.

params.name: voiceChannelId
params.description: The unique identifier of the voice channel where the signaling exchange is taking place.

params.name: receiverUserId
params.description: The unique local identifier of the user who is the intended recipient of this signaling message.

params.name: signalId
params.description: A unique identifier for this specific WebRTC signaling message.

firestore.reasoning:
The recommended Firestore structure is designed to support real-time WebRTC signaling and user presence tracking while strictly adhering to the specified design principles, particularly Authorization Independence given the absence of Firebase Authentication.The core approach involves segmenting data by `voiceChannelId` and further by `userId` or `receiverUserId` within those channels.

**Authorization Independence (CRITICAL):**
Since Firebase Authentication is explicitly forbidden, `request.auth.uid` will not be available in Firestore security rules. This is a critical constraint that shifts the burden of identity verification. To still achieve a semblance of authorization independence and debuggable rules, the design assumes that the client-provided `userId` (generated and stored in `localStorage`) will be *the* identifier that security rules can compare against fields in documents or path parameters. For this to work in practice, the application would likely need to pass this `userId` with every Firestore request in a way that rules can access it (e.g., through a custom token or App Check with custom claims, though the prompt implies a simpler setup). Assuming this `current_user_id` is available in rules:

1.  **`voiceChannels/{voiceChannelId}/presence/{userId}`:** The `userId` is part of the document's path *and* explicitly stored within the `UserPresence` document itself (`definition.params.userId` and `UserPresence.userId`). The `voiceChannelId` is also in the path and document. This denormalization means that rules can directly verify ownership (`request.params.userId == current_user_id`) without needing to fetch a parent document. Any user wanting to update their presence simply targets their own path.
2.  **`voiceChannels/{voiceChannelId}/users/{receiverUserId}/webrtcSignals/{signalId}`:** The `receiverUserId` is crucial and is embedded in the path (`definition.params.receiverUserId`). This creates a dedicated 'mailbox' subcollection for each user within a channel. `senderUserId` is also explicitly stored in the `WebRTCSignal` document. This denormalization allows rules to check `request.params.receiverUserId == current_user_id` for read access (ensuring a user can only read their own signals) and `request.resource.data.senderUserId == current_user_id` for write access (preventing sender spoofing). Both checks are independent of parent document lookups.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**
The structure inherently supports secure and efficient `list` operations (Query-Applies-Permissions):

1.  **`/voiceChannels/{voiceChannelId}`:** This collection is public/read-only for all users (or all users with a `current_user_id`). `list` operations will retrieve all predefined channels without needing rule-based filtering, satisfying QAP.
2.  **`/voiceChannels/{voiceChannelId}/presence`:** When a user joins a `voiceChannelId`, they will query this subcollection to see who else is present. The `voiceChannelId` in the path directly scopes the query to the relevant channel. Rules can then permit `list` access if the `current_user_id` also has a presence record in that channel (meaning they are a participant). This allows a `list` to return exactly the set of users allowed, without server-side filtering on non-indexed fields.
3.  **`/voiceChannels/{voiceChannelId}/users/{receiverUserId}/webrtcSignals`:** A user subscribes to their own signaling mailbox to receive messages. The query `db.collection('voiceChannels/{channelId}/users/{currentUserId}/webrtcSignals')` is naturally scoped by both `channelId` and `currentUserId`. Rules would restrict read access to `request.params.receiverUserId == current_user_id`. This means the query itself defines the scope, and the rules confirm the permission without needing to filter the results, perfectly aligning with QAPs.
